facts.text: Jack Rittenhouse noted San Fidel as a Route 66 landmark in his Guidebook to the U.S., highlighting the town’s historic roadside appeal.
The Acoma Curio Shop, an adobe building from 1937, sits on the National Register of Historic Places and once sold Native American crafts before closing in WWII.
In 1868, Baltazar Jaramillo founded the first settlement at La Vega de San Jose, the seed that grew into modern San Fidel.
Spanish colonial land grants issued from the late 17th century onward shaped San Fidel’s early development, creating ranchos that served as buffers against nearby pueblos.
Joseph Mission School, founded over a century ago by Franciscan friars, served as a mission parish for the Acoma and Laguna pueblos.
San Fidel sits at 6,174 feet above sea level, giving it a high‑altitude desert climate.
